chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluyah (may God be pleased with him) narrated be pleased with him) narrated from his uncle Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Kufi, from Ibn Fazal, from Abdullah ibn Maymun, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

For the adulterer are six characteristics: three in this world and three in the Hereafter. As for those in this world, the light of his face fades, he inherits poverty, and his destruction is hastened. And as for those in the Hereafter: the Wrath of the Lord (may His Majesty be Exalted), a bad Reckoning, and eternal residence in the Fire.
ai.seo_question: What are the six characteristics or consequences of adultery according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq records this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) to categorize the spiritual and physical decay caused by adultery, emphasizing that the sin corrupts both the inner light of the face and the soul's standing before God. This tripartite division reflects the Shia theological understanding of how major sins manifest as immediate worldly afflictions and delayed Hereafter punishments, serving as a deterrent for the believer.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 6-4 Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluyih - may God be pleased with him - narrated that his uncle Muhammad ibn Abil-Qasim quoted Muhammad ibn Ali al-Kufy, on the authority of Ibn Fazal, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Maymun that Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB) said,

“There are six characteristics for an adulterer three of which are in this world and three in the Hereafter. Those which are in this world are: the brightness of his face would fade away; he will inherit poverty and his destruction will be speeded up. And the three which are for the Hereafter are: the Wrath of the Lord - may His Majesty be Exalted; a hard Reckoning; and residing in the Fire.”
